title: Grand Principality of Serbia
capsule: The Grand Principality of Serbia, centered on Raška, emerged under the Vukanović branch of the Vojislavljević dynasty when Grand Župan Vukan, installed by Duklja's King Constantine Bodin around 1083, asserted increasing independence from Byzantium in the 1090s, raiding imperial territory in Kosovo and Macedonia before submitting hostages to Emperor Alexios I. His successors, including Uroš I and the rival brothers Uroš II and Desa, ruled through recurring Byzantine intervention and dynastic infighting across the early-to-mid twelfth century, at times marrying into the Hungarian royal house to counterbalance Constantinople. The fractious succession was finally resolved in 1166-1169 when Stefan Nemanja, backed by his brothers, overturned the brief rule of Tihomir to found the Nemanjić dynasty that would dominate later medieval Serbia.
